body:
Merged origin/main (a6e9c7c: #332 / #327 non-finite WCS, #333 / #257 program comments, #367 / #298) into the branch, now at 115bdd7. GitHub reports MERGEABLE. The PR stays a draft.

**Conflicts**
- `commands/set_wcs.rs`: kept #342's one-WCS signature `SetWcsOrigin::new(world, location)` and added #332's checks for a non-finite rotation, a zero-norm rotation and a non-finite origin. The refusal now names the active setup's WCS by its label, e.g. `WCS (G55): rotation must be finite (check the angle inputs)`, instead of `work offset G55`.
- `setup_sheet/sections.rs`: kept the single `WCS (G5x)` line and the program offset taken from the setup, and added #332's rotated / not-finite line under it.

**Semantic ports git did not flag**
- `tests/rotated_wcs.rs`: #332's command test placed a G55 slot. It now labels Setup1 G55, places its one WCS and asserts `WCS (G55)` for all five cases. The post-gate checks now read `the WCS (G54) has a non-finite placement`, which is the wording the one-WCS gate already writes.
- `project/validate.rs`: the load refusal now reads `WCS '<name>' has a non-finite or degenerate placement`.
- `tests/one_wcs.rs`: new test `a_v53_posted_slot_with_a_degenerate_rotation_is_refused_after_the_rung`. It pins that #332's load check still runs on the slot a v53 file posted after the v53 -> v54 rung moves it (the check runs after `wcs_one::settle`).
- `docs/decisions/327-nonfinite-wcs-rotation.md`: wording updated to match.

**Gate (worktree target, debug)**
- app lib: 92 passed.
- Suites, all passing: one_wcs 8, setup_wcs 7, setup_defines_wcs 4, rotated_wcs 9, wcs_align 5, setups 11, setup_sheet 7, posting 17, project_roundtrip 69, commands_undo 32, golden_cl 23, conformance 6, fanuc_post 8, mcp 4, program_comments 4, heidenhain_block_form 4, regression_models 2.
- ui lib (CWD crates/ui): 297 passed, 2 ignored. No snapshot changes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 115bdd72e2a4c2dee47e7248110b4f7273247b14 -->
Clean - ready to merge

Independent check of the merge 115bdd7 (parents d016790 = branch, a6e9c7c = main with #332/#327) against #332's own change. Static review of the diff; the suites were not rebuilt (author reports them green).

1. Every #332 refusal survives: SetWcsOrigin::new refuses non-finite rotation, zero-norm rotation and non-finite origin (commands/set_wcs.rs); the post gate refuses a non-finite or zero-norm/NaN placement by name (posting_wcs_rotation.rs, offset_frame NonFinite); project load refuses a non-finite or degenerate offset placement (project/validate.rs). None dropped or weakened.
2. SetWcsOrigin::new(world, location) is kept; the slot argument and the slot-based wcs_entity_name(world, setup, slot) are gone. No slot API returned.
3. Messages use the "WCS (G55)" label at SetWcsOrigin and in the setup sheet and post refusals ("the WCS (G54) has a non-finite placement", "setup X: its WCS (G55)"). No "work offset G55", no Auto/default/inferred wording in any refusal added by the merge. Nit, not a blocker: the load-time message (validate.rs) names the entity ("WCS 'G55' ...") because the loader has no setup label; it is not the label form but it is not misleading.
4. rotated_wcs.rs ports all five #332 tests one for one: the same five SetWcsOrigin cases, the same three NaN rotation cases in the post gate, the same origin case, the same project-load check (zero-norm rotation refused, saved rotated file still loads), the same setup-sheet assertions (the rotation line text is byte-identical). Only the expected wording changed (work offset G54 becomes the WCS (G54) label, and the entity-name form at load). Test count 4 -> 9 on the branch side, #332 added 5, the merged file has those 5.
5. a_v53_posted_slot_with_a_degenerate_rotation_is_refused_after_the_rung makes sense: the v53 -> v54 rung (wcs_one::settle) keeps the posted entity under its name and runs before validate_kind, so the zero-norm rotation on G55 is refused by name on the migrated dto. The test pins that the #327 check survives the migration path.
6. render_wcs prints the WCS line and, when the offset is turned or non-finite, the rotation line (same wording as #332); the program offset line is kept.

Checks: no conflict markers in the merged tree; no unwrap/expect/panic added in non-test code by the merge; the changed files are under 400 lines; the merge diff against main removes only the slot-era lines it replaces.

Not blocking, pre-existing and outside this merge: commands/setup_wcs.rs still says "work offset #i does not exist - the slots are G54 to G59" (unchanged by the merge).

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$3.62 (rough estimate from size: 1769 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
